title: TaskCompleted Verify-Gate Bypass via Empty Git Commit
capability_defeated: The task-completed-verify.sh gate is supposed to enforce compile + test before Claude can declare a task done. An empty git commit (git commit --allow-empty) produces a zero-line diff from all four git queries on lines 19-23. The guard on line 25 (`if [ -z "$changed" ]; then exit 0`) treats empty-diff as 'no code changed — skip verification entirely' and exits 0 unconditionally, even when the working tree contains a package.json with failing tests. The agent can claim 'fix: resolved type errors' and the hook passes without running pnpm test or pnpm tsc.
attack_scenario: Agent makes real code edits (which would fail tests), commits them, then issues a second empty commit with a plausible fix message. TaskCompleted fires on the second commit. The gate sees an empty HEAD~1..HEAD diff, exits 0, and the task is marked done. No tests run.

setup: git config user.email t@t.com && git config user.name T
verify: git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD   # → empty output
echo EXIT=$?   # → EXIT=0  (gate passed, no tests ran)
reproduction.expected_output: EXIT=2 (test gate should have fired pnpm test → exit 1)

root_cause: Lines 17-36 of task-completed-verify.sh compute 'changed' by unioning four git queries: HEAD~1..HEAD diff, unstaged diff, staged diff, and untracked files. When the most-recent commit is empty AND the working tree is clean, all four queries return empty strings. The guard `if [ -z "$changed" ]; then exit 0` was intended to skip verification when there are genuinely no code changes (e.g., docs-only session). It has no awareness that the PREVIOUS commit (or any earlier work) may contain failing code — it only looks at the delta from the empty commit. The fix is to additionally check whether the HEAD commit itself is an empty commit (git diff-tree --no-commit-id -r HEAD produces no output) and, if so, walk back to HEAD~1 or refuse to pass.

novelty_vs_prior_findings.F1_F11_rounds_1_2: All prior findings targeted PreToolUse hooks (bash-egress-guard, protect-sensitive-reads, git-safety refspec, mcp-guard trust classification). This is the first finding against the TaskCompleted gate — a different hook event entirely.
novelty_vs_prior_findings.recon_G12_G13: G12/G13 targeted mcp-audit-log.sh PostToolUse (verb-allowlist gaps) and mcp-calls-log.sh (cut -d_ trust misclassification). This finding is orthogonal: it defeats verification enforcement, not audit logging.
novelty_vs_prior_findings.key_distinction: Prior bypasses let an attacker DO something undetected. This bypass lets an attacker CLAIM completion without verification — the trust model around 'task is done' is defeated, not just the audit trail.

secondary_leads.title: Audit Gap: 9 SILENT mutating bridge-db/engraph tools
secondary_leads.detail: mcp-audit-log.sh skips logging when the tool name matches the read-only pattern OR fails to match the mutating-verb pattern. Tools named with neither pattern — confirm_shipped_sync, mark_shipped_processed, pick_up_handoff, clear_handoff, save_snapshot, record_cost, export_bridge_markdown, sync_from_file (bridge-db) and append, archive, unarchive, move_note, setup, migrate_apply, migrate_undo (engraph) — execute with NO mutation-audit record. These are all real state-mutating operations: approving shipped events, clearing handoffs, mutating the SecondBrain vault. The gap exists because the mutating-verb allowlist was designed for generic CRUD verbs (create/update/delete) and did not enumerate domain-specific operation names. Reproduction: invoke mcp__bridge_db__confirm_shipped_sync or mcp__engraph__archive and check ~/.claude/logs/mcp-mutations.jsonl — no line is appended.
secondary_leads.impact: MEDIUM — attacker can confirm, archive, or migrate vault content without a mutation-audit trail

secondary_leads.title: Trust Misclassification: claude_ai_* and plugin_* servers → third_party
secondary_leads.detail: mcp-calls-log.sh extracts the server name via `cut -d'_' -f3` (line 21). The MCP tool name format is mcp__<server>__<tool>, where <server> uses hyphens not underscores. For servers whose registered name contains underscores — all claude_ai_* tools (Google Drive, Vercel, Cloudflare) and plugin_* tools (context-mode, context7) — cut -d'_' extracts only the third underscore-delimited field: 'claude' for claude_ai_Google_Drive__create_file, 'plugin' for plugin_context-mode. Neither 'claude' nor 'plugin' appears in the trust-class lookup table, so all these calls are logged as trust_class: third_party instead of their actual classification. A security reviewer reading the log would conclude these are untrusted third-party calls and might ignore or deprioritize them, while a genuine third-party tool that happens to use a simple name like 'bridge-db' would be classified as local. The fix is to split on the double-underscore __ delimiter rather than single underscore.
secondary_leads.impact: LOW-MEDIUM — misleads audit log consumers; no direct bypass but degrades trust-aware monitoring

refuted_leads.hypothesis: subagent-quality-gate.sh injection via crafted subagent output
refuted_leads.verdict: REFUTED — low impact. The gate reads last_assistant_message and applies grep pattern matches. Even if a subagent crafts output containing jq-special characters or newlines, the gate only outputs a block/allow decision via jq -n (not user-supplied interpolation). The PROSE_MSG variable is passed to grep, not to jq --arg, so jq injection is not possible. The sed strip on line 24 handles code fences. No meaningful injection surface found.
refuted_leads.residual: A subagent whose output begins with a line matching '^(permission denied|timed out)' (line 35) gets blocked even if it succeeded — false-positive DoS is possible but is not an attacker-controlled escalation.

refuted_leads.verdict: CONFIRMED ADVISORY ONLY. The hook is wired as async: true under UserPromptSubmit and returns additionalContext (not permissionDecision: deny). It cannot block execution. Confirmed by settings.json wiring and hook output format (line 68: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext). Zero blocking capability — as the prompt suspected.

refuted_leads.hypothesis: session-end-bridge-log.sh poisoning via CWD or PROJECT
refuted_leads.verdict: LOW IMPACT. PROJECT=basename(CWD) is passed as a CLI argument to `uv run python -m bridge_db --log-session-boundary PROJECT`. Shell injection would require CWD to contain shell metacharacters, which macOS/APFS paths rarely do. The ARGS array construction (line 29) uses proper bash array quoting, so the argument is safely passed. No practical injection surface.
